# `react/rules-of-hooks`

**Hooks are called at the top level of components and hooks**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-react` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-react` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (moving a hook can change what the code does on the renders that skipped it) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.1.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` |

## What it checks

Hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, any `use…`) are called only at the top level of a function component
or a custom hook: not in conditions, loops, nested functions, after an early return, in classes, or
in plain functions.

**Why:** React matches hook calls to state by their order, so a hook that runs on some renders and
not others mixes up every hook after it.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-react
pip install codelaw-rules-react
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:react/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:react/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"react/rules-of-hooks" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "react/rules-of-hooks" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"react/rules-of-hooks" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"react/rules-of-hooks" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"react/rules-of-hooks" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "react/rules-of-hooks": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore react/rules-of-hooks: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore react/rules-of-hooks expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule react/rules-of-hooks --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain react/rules-of-hooks       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule react/rules-of-hooks  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>        # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the hook call to the top level of the component or hook, before any early return.
2. Put the condition inside the hook (e.g. inside the effect) instead of around it.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
function Profile({ id }) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  const [user] = useState(null);
  return user;
}
```

#### Do

```js
function Profile({ id }) {
  const [user] = useState(null);
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return user;
}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  const [user] = useState(null);
  return user;
}
```

#### Do

```jsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  const [user] = useState(null);
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return user;
}
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
function useProfile(id: string) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return useState(id);
}
```

#### Do

```ts
function useProfile(id: string) {
  const state = useState(id);
  return id ? state : null;
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  const [user] = useState(null);
  return user;
}
```

#### Do

```tsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  const [user] = useState(null);
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return user;
}
```
